 By Ira Winderman | iwinderman@sunsentinel.com | South Florida Sun Sentinel PUBLISHED: October 30, 2026 at 6:05 AM EDT | UPDATED: October 30, 2026 at 8:30 AM EDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Q: At some point Erik Spoelstra has to start Pelle Larsson over Klay Thompson. And Bobby Portis has been good, as well. – Brian. 
 A: But it also doesn’t mean you necessarily have to start your best players. It’s also about being able to cycle through a rotation, with both Pelle Larsson and Bobby Portis Jr. assuredly to get ample playing time alongside Giannis Antetokounmpo. As long as Klay Thompson continues to draw the attention of the defense and space the floor, he still is a positive asset. And Bam Adebayo is not coming out of the starting lineup. Period. But it’s not as if Erik Spoelstra also hasn’t already made subtle changes, with Klay’s minutes reduced, Tim Hardaway Jr. not with quite as large a role as initially forecast, and Nikola Jovic held out of the second half Wednesday night in Atlanta after making his midcourt buzzer-beater at the end of that first half.

 Q: It is time to shake things up. Giannis Antetokounmpo is not a traditional center nor is Bam Adebayo. Nick Richards showed me a great deal of hustle and toughness and athleticism in the preseason. It may be time for the Heat to start him with Giannis as a typical NBA lineup. Giannis thrived with Brooks Lopez behind him in Milwaukee. Lets see some slam dunks instead of all the missed 3-pointers. Sit down Klay Thompson as he is past his prime, an inconsistent shooter and a detriment on defense. Other teams go right at him as they used to do with Duncan Robinson. Play Bobby Portis Jr. more as he is a solid shooter and high energy on defense. Lets face it we are not great 3-point shooters and we need the points to come from somewhere either on defense or at the basket.  – Irwin, Boynton Beach. 
 A: Appreciate the suggestions and the thought of needing something different amid this 1-4 start. But Giannis Antetokounmpo is one thing on offense – a downhill driver from the middle of the court. So the last thing, the very last thing, you need is a big man clogging the middle of the lane. And it’s not as if Nick Richards can be positioned anywhere else (the dunker spot is possible, but even that brings another defender to that area). What you need is a big man alongside who can stretch or at least space the floor, as Brook Lopez did in Milwaukee with his 3-point shooting. But that also is a problem when Bam Adebayo attempts to force the issue from beyond the arc.
 Q: Bam Adebayo can be frustrating because he focuses on contributing to the team (defense) and not scoring. Giannis Antetokounmpo is a student of the game, so couldn’t he learn how to quarterback the defense while Bam scores and vice-a-versa?  Then one would play a rebounder/defender while the other scores.  They are so versatile that they could drive opponents crazy with their hybrid abilities.  – Eric, Miami. 
 A: No, no, no, no, no. Giannis Antetokounmpo is an all-time elite scorer. It is why he was so coveted. You don’t take the ball out of the hands of a player like that. What you do is make that the starting point and then do everything around Giannis’ scoring. The Heat do not need Giannis to do a little of everything. They need him to do a lot of scoring (and rebounding).
